summary.oneLiner:
DCB Bank delivered its **highest-ever quarterly profit of INR 184.74 crores** while absorbing a **INR 26.87 crores
one-time new-Labour-Code charge** — ex that charge, PAT would have been **INR 205 crores**, ROA **1.01%** and ROE
**14.10%**, i.e. the bank has effectively reached the 1% ROA mark that has been its multi-year goalpost. The engine
is a deposit-cost story, not a yield story: cost of deposit fell to **6.86%** (−10 bps QoQ) while borrowings were
almost halved from **INR 8,400 crores to about INR 4,700 crores**, lifting NIM to **3.27%** even as yield on advances
fell faster than funding cost on lagged repo transmission. Underwriting is simultaneously the cleanest in years —
**slippage 3.08% and GNPA 2.72%, both the lowest in 18 quarters; NNPA 1.1%, lowest in 11 quarters; credit cost 0.37%**
against a stated 0.45% floor — achieved with **fewer employees than a year ago (10,981 vs 11,339)** on 18.5% advance
growth. The open sores management itself names are the **flatlining current account** and the **stuck INR 2,200 crore
SME book**.

order book & pipeline:
Not applicable in the industrial sense (bank). The lending-pipeline read management gave:

- **Demand is borrower-led, not lender-push.** Asked directly whether SME growth is lenders being happy to lend or
  borrowers genuinely wanting credit: "Clearly, I would tell you, **it's a latter. It is that there is a requirement.
  There is a hunger.**"
- **Login volumes at a seasonal peak out of season:** "**December logins are very, very similar to March log-ins.**
  And March is usually a special month… We are neck to neck on that." But: "**Conversion still is a bit more
  conservative.**"
- **Competitive intensity is visible in leakage:** "us losing our good portfolio customers to competition for a higher
  exposure or for a lower cost… If we don't, if you're not able to disburse in time, customers have multiple offers,
  and they're going away."
- **Geographic breadth:** "It's not region specific, **across India**, I'm finding that there is an increased demand.
  And when you speak to DSAs also, you are seeing the same thing happening."
- **System context (analyst-supplied, undisputed):** aggregate system credit off-take back to ~14–14.5%.
segment / subsidiary detail:
- **Mortgages — ~INR 28,000 crore book, 51% of advances (was 54% four-to-six quarters ago), grew only 12.4% YoY.**
  Three deliberate management actions, all described in the past tense ("I'm using past tense because it's already
  done"): (1) **reorient from Home Loan to Business Loan** — HL is now **less than 50%** of mortgage, and **BL is
  "even more than 60% of the incremental sourcing"**; (2) **raise average ticket size** from "approximately INR 27
  lakhs going to INR 32 lakhs… that INR 5 lakh actually is a **19% growth**"; (3) **shift from DSA-originated to
  own-originated** — "their sourcing, the contribution to DCB Bank has come down. With any national DSA, you can
  check it out." Kutty's framing: "we are **changing the wheels of a moving train**."
- **SME — INR 2,249 crores, the acknowledged laggard.** "we are, in a way, **struggling on the SME book**… it has been
  **stuck at the INR 2,200 crores level for some time now**." The new mid-segment vertical (**INR 3 crores to INR 15
  crores** tickets) is "in an **embryonic stage**" — live in **four locations, six more to come**, NSM and RSMs hired;
  "you'll see the impact of it happening in about, I don't know, **3, 4 quarters' time**… This is a long game."
- **Co-lending — 16% of the asset book, down from 16.22% in Q2.** "largely **gold loan**. Multiple players, but largely
  gold loan based." Growth decelerating by design: "we grew **108% last year**, currently, we are at about **60%, 65%**"
  and from FY27 it tracks total book growth. **New CLM-1 co-lending rules effective 1 January 2026**: "you're aware
  that from January 1 onwards, we have had this new CLM 1 new rules of co-lending coming into play. We see that this
  will continue."
- **"Others" under advances — INR 2,000 crores.** "It's not a large book… the largest component here will be about
  **INR 600 crores, INR 700 crores of loan against term deposit**. So there is a mixed bag of whatever is not
  mentioned in the other products."
- **Deposits.** Cost base "almost INR 65,000 crores". Retail-to-bulk mix **unchanged**: "our ratio of retail to bulk
  remains the same at the portfolio level. And there is no reason to believe that it will be any different" — and the
  rate cut was symmetric, "the reduction in the rate of interest for both bulk deposits and retail deposits, Q3 over
  Q2 is practically the same."
- **Niyo channel — 0.5 million customers.** "a pretty good base of Niyo customers who have come in for us, primarily
  for **low-cost forex card** purposes… cross-selling the savings account and deposit to them is a big opportunity…
  **not a traditional self-employed customer**… primarily salaried and definitely affluent and high net worth."

6a. moat & competitive position:
Evidenced on this call — kept here only, not repeated above:

- **Cost position built from headcount deflation, not scale.** 18.5% advance and 19.5% deposit growth delivered with
  **10,981 employees vs 11,339 a year earlier**, and cost-to-income *down* YoY (61.84%) *despite* absorbing INR 26.87
  crores of one-off wage cost. Named drivers: "**organic sourcing vis-à-vis DSA source business, vendor renegotiation,
  impact of digitalization and improved use of AI**". Only 5 branches opened in 9M.
- **Sourcing-channel economics — a genuine durability advantage, quantified qualitatively.** "**the non-DSA sourced
  accounts stay with you for far longer than DSA sourced accounts.** In some cases, **you don't even recover the cost
  of valuation and legal and account fulfillment** by the time the customer forecloses and goes away. And with the
  **zero foreclosure charges** in many cases, there is hardly any recovery possible. So from a long-term perspective,
  this is the way to go." This is a switching-cost / customer-lifetime moat being deliberately bought at the price of
  near-term mortgage growth (12.4% vs 18–20% bank growth).
- **Deposit-pricing power in the making — measured, not asserted.** DCB is converting from a price-leader to a
  service-led franchise: "for the last let's say, about 10, 15 years… **the reason to buy has always been price. That's
  changing.**" The metric offered: "**The difference between our retail peak rate and the composite highest peak rate
  of six biggest banks in India is now down to 60 bps. So we're converging.**" Combined with top-20 concentration at
  **6.61%**, this is the "all three together" test management sets itself: "it is **not 2 out of 3, or 1 out of 3, it's
  all the 3 together, all the time**" (cost of deposit, growth, granularity).
- **ECL readiness as a compliance moat.** Parallel-run for "**Almost 4 years**" (Ravi Kumar) — "**it doesn't keep you
  awake in the night**… It's more or less in line… honestly, when you look at it, there's **hardly anything to worry
  about**." Note the asymmetry management itself flags: "**you will not be able to get a benefit. You'll only, it's the
  higher of the two.**"
- **Underwriting vintage quality.** "**Post pandemic, this is perhaps the best few quarters I've seen in terms of new
  vintage bouncing**" — with recoveries & upgrades at 86% of fresh flow.
margins & cost dynamics:
- **The margin is a liability-side story, and management said so directly:** "the **NIM growth is fully predicated on
  our term deposits and our savings account interest rate going southward**. And we have clarity and we have done this
  playbook once, not once twice, for the last 2 quarters."
- **Spread compressed QoQ and management did not dispute it** — yield on advances −13 bps vs cost of deposit −10 bps.
  Explanation: "The **full impact of the 50 bps rate cut** which happened in the previous quarter **is taken in Q3**,
  the full impact. So what you're seeing is a **lagged impact**. For the 25 basis points repo rate cut, which happened
  in Q3, the impact you will see happening in Q4."
- **Two opposing Q4 FY26 forces (both now history):** "The **full impact of CRR is not boxed in yet. That's a positive
  for Q4**, what is not so very positive is that the **full impact of the 25 basis point repo cut has also not been
  boxed in**."
- **The borrowing swap is doing quiet, heavy lifting.** "our ability to get lower cost of deposit **by giving away
  borrowing, which is more expensive**, is coming into play very quickly. And that's also one of the reasons why…
  the balance sheet is growing only 14%, whereas… we are growing our key areas of customer deposits and loans and
  advances at a much, much higher pace." Also: "the **fall in cost of deposit is sharper than the fall in cost of
  funds**, which basically means that the impact of cost of borrowing is much lesser."
- **The savings-rate lever is nearly exhausted; the term-deposit lever is not.** The 16 bps → 10 bps deceleration in
  cost-of-deposit reduction "is the impact of savings account cut… **you can't cut deeper than what you're cutting.
  Currently, we're at 1.5% at the lowest end of the scale**… you will get the benefit from **TD going forward**."
- **Operating jaws are positive:** "**The jaws are widening** with income growing at 16% and expenses, **including the
  onetime**, growing at 15%."
- **Fee is deposit-linked, not loan-linked — an under-appreciated structural point management volunteered:** "our fee
  growth is **less linked to loans. It is more linked to deposits**… third-party distribution, which is more liability
  linked. Trade finance, largely still liability linked, FX income is DCB remit, foreign remittance… ATM fees, again,
  liabilities. So… **we don't even link it to the loan growth.**"
capex / expansion (watch slippage):
- **Branch expansion was throttled through 9M FY26 and is being restarted:** only **5 branches opened in nine months**;
  "Next year, we should be touching the **500 branches mark**. So that most likely will happen."
- **Headcount inflected within the quarter:** "if you see Q2 to Q3, there has been a **slight increase in the number of
  people**, while we're still lesser than the number of people we had a year back or in March."
- **Explicitly "both", not a trade-off:** "**it is not one or the other, it is both**. A large proportion of our
  benefits will come from efficiency improvement, from increased digitization. And, but that doesn't mean that we will
  not increase the number of people. **We are still people dependent in terms of our growth, specifically assets.**"
- **Efficiency is framed as permanent, not a phase:** "improving efficiency, going digital, **war on paper**, these are
  not epithets or slogan… **we'll live and die by it**… there's **no finish line** there."
- **SME vertical build-out:** four locations live, **six more to open**, meaningful impact only in "3, 4 quarters".
- **Slippage risk to watch (now scoreable):** the 500-branch mark and the 18%+ mortgage re-acceleration were both
  pinned to **FY27**, and the co-lending ≤15% commitment to **31-Mar-2026** — all now verifiable against actuals.
capital allocation:

  infusion**… **right now, there is no urgency for capital. But for future growth, we require it.**"
- **Trigger framework is dual:** "We have both as a **timeline based as well as event based**. We are pretty much clear

- **Internal accretion is the stated bridge:** "if you're able to **increase your book value by INR 5 every quarter**
  for the last n number of quarters. And in the future also, we are reasonably confident about repeating our business
  in a similar fashion."
- **RWA discipline:** RWA +5% on 7% QoQ asset growth; "Our RWA is well below the 50% mark."
- **Balance-sheet mix as capital allocation:** deliberately shrinking expensive borrowings (INR 8,400 cr → ~INR 4,700

- **Co-lending capped as a risk-allocation choice:** "We're **comfortable with 15%**."
risks & watch-items:
1. **Regulatory risk to insurance commissions — the single largest named threat to the fee engine.** Third-party
   distribution is the biggest core-fee driver and "**a big component in our fee structure**"; the analyst framed the
   risk as regulators "considering **reducing the commissions that are payable on insurance product**… there has been
   a lot of articles on this and I think **some regulatory movement** also." Management did not deny the risk — it
   answered with the mitigation (trade finance). Also hedged the fee guide: core fee holds "**unless there's some
   regulatory action happening, which one is not aware of**."
2. **Deposit-gathering under a changed value proposition.** "close to **3,000 odd employees** in the Branch Banking
   system are now fighting a battle in the market where the reason for coming to us is **not the pricing alone**…
   **So people are finding it a bit difficult.**" M.B. Mahesh's framing was pointed: "in the past, in a slightly
   difficult deposit environment, usually DCB had stormed it, its cost of funds kind of growing faster. **We seem to
   be heading into one such situation again.**"
3. **Current account flatlining** — self-identified, unresolved, and multi-effect (cost of deposit + trade fee + SME).
   "**That we haven't got an action going is another matter.**"
4. **SME book stuck at ~INR 2,200 crores** with the fix admittedly 3–4 quarters out.
5. **Mortgage growth deficit** — 12.4% vs an 18–20% bank; the recovery is a promise for FY27, and it depends on people
   internalising a new model ("people take time to get used to the new way of thinking").
6. **Merchant OD / relationship strategy behind schedule** — "still in the infancy… I haven't seen real good progress
   happening yet", payoff 12–18 months out.
7. **Further repo cuts cut both ways.** The NIM-up thesis holds "**unless some repo rate action is done by RBI**";
   conversely the SA lever is dead without another cut. Yield repricing leads deposit repricing on the way down.
8. **NNPA still above the 1% self-set line** (1.1%), and slippage at 3.08% — best in 18 quarters, but an absolute level
   that leaves no room for a credit-cycle turn.
9. **Capital raise / dilution** is stated as a matter of when, not if.
10. **CLM-1 co-lending regime (live from 1-Jan-2026)** with the book being actively cut from 16.22% → ≤15%.
11. **ECL transition** — no benefit possible, only a floor ("it's the **higher of the two**"), though management is
    relaxed after a ~4-year parallel run.
12. **Zero foreclosure charges** structurally impair recovery of acquisition cost on short-lived (DSA-sourced) loans.
13. **Guidance-vs-arithmetic gap flagged by an analyst and NOT numerically rebutted:** 9M-annualised ROE ~12.5–12.6%
    against the 13.5% FY27 / 14.5% FY28 path. Management's answer was a process answer ("consistency… predictability"),
    plus the correct point that no FY26 ROE guidance was ever given.

Confident, unusually plain-spoken, and — notably — **volunteers its own failures unprompted**. Kutty flagged the OD

non-obvious takeaways:
- **The fee book is a liability franchise in disguise.** Management's clearest structural insight, offered
  unprompted: DCB's fee scales with **deposits, not loans** (third-party distribution, trade finance, FX/remittance,
  ATM). This inverts the usual bank fee model, means the CA/deposit gap is a *revenue* problem rather than only a
  *cost* problem, and explains why current account is "very, very high on my priority list."
- **DCB is a `Financialization` BENEFICIARY, not a victim** — the opposite side of the trade from the PSU/old-private
  banks in this corpus. Where BANKINDIA and J&KBANK name household savings migrating into equity/MF as the cause of
  their CASA erosion, DCB's largest single core-fee driver **is** that migration ("a very decent third-party
  distribution fee income"). Same macro, opposite P&L line — worth carrying into any cross-bank theme view.
- **The 14% balance-sheet growth is a feature, not weakness.** A screener reading DCB on total-asset growth sees a
  decelerating bank; the 18.5%/19.5% customer growth is being masked by the deliberate retirement of INR 3,700 crores
  of expensive borrowings. The gap between the two numbers *is* the margin strategy.
- **The mortgage slowdown is self-inflicted and paid for in advance.** 12.4% growth is the price of three simultaneous
  changes (HL→BL, ticket size up, DSA→organic) that were completed ~9 months ago. If management is right about
  non-DSA loan longevity, the growth deficit is a timing cost against a permanent lifetime-value gain — and the ticket
  size already moved 19%.
- **Slippage 3.08% being an 18-quarter *low* is a reminder of the underlying asset class.** This is a self-employed,
  small-ticket, secured book; the improvement is real (86% recovery-and-upgrade rate, best post-pandemic vintage
  bouncing) but the absolute level is high by universal-bank standards.
- **Management explicitly refuted the commodity-price → working-capital-credit thesis.** An analyst offered it;
  Kutty rejected it for his segment — the uptick is in **installment loans, not CC/OD**. A useful negative datapoint
  for anyone modelling an SME working-capital cycle off commodity prices.
- **The co-lending book is a gold-loan proxy being deliberately shrunk** — 108% → 60–65% → bank-growth-rate, and
  16.22% → ≤15% of assets. Any read of DCB's growth quality should net this out.
- **ULI + land-record digitisation is an unpriced option on a mortgage lender's cost curve** — management called it
  "the game changer" and said "we are involved in it", with no timeline or quantum.
- **A rare disclosure of channel-economics failure:** on some DSA-sourced loans "you don't even recover the cost of

non-obvious takeaways:
- **The fee book is a liability franchise in disguise.** Management's clearest structural insight, offered
  unprompted: DCB's fee scales with **deposits, not loans** (third-party distribution, trade finance, FX/remittance,
  ATM). This inverts the usual bank fee model, means the CA/deposit gap is a *revenue* problem rather than only a
  *cost* problem, and explains why current account is "very, very high on my priority list."
- **DCB is a `Financialization` BENEFICIARY, not a victim** — the opposite side of the trade from the PSU/old-private
  banks in this corpus. Where BANKINDIA and J&KBANK name household savings migrating into equity/MF as the cause of
  their CASA erosion, DCB's largest single core-fee driver **is** that migration ("a very decent third-party
  distribution fee income"). Same macro, opposite P&L line — worth carrying into any cross-bank theme view.
- **The 14% balance-sheet growth is a feature, not weakness.** A screener reading DCB on total-asset growth sees a
  decelerating bank; the 18.5%/19.5% customer growth is being masked by the deliberate retirement of INR 3,700 crores
  of expensive borrowings. The gap between the two numbers *is* the margin strategy.
- **The mortgage slowdown is self-inflicted and paid for in advance.** 12.4% growth is the price of three simultaneous
  changes (HL→BL, ticket size up, DSA→organic) that were completed ~9 months ago. If management is right about
  non-DSA loan longevity, the growth deficit is a timing cost against a permanent lifetime-value gain — and the ticket
  size already moved 19%.
- **Slippage 3.08% being an 18-quarter *low* is a reminder of the underlying asset class.** This is a self-employed,
  small-ticket, secured book; the improvement is real (86% recovery-and-upgrade rate, best post-pandemic vintage
  bouncing) but the absolute level is high by universal-bank standards.
- **Management explicitly refuted the commodity-price → working-capital-credit thesis.** An analyst offered it;
  Kutty rejected it for his segment — the uptick is in **installment loans, not CC/OD**. A useful negative datapoint
  for anyone modelling an SME working-capital cycle off commodity prices.
- **The co-lending book is a gold-loan proxy being deliberately shrunk** — 108% → 60–65% → bank-growth-rate, and
  16.22% → ≤15% of assets. Any read of DCB's growth quality should net this out.
- **ULI + land-record digitisation is an unpriced option on a mortgage lender's cost curve** — management called it
  "the game changer" and said "we are involved in it", with no timeline or quantum.
- **A rare disclosure of channel-economics failure:** on some DSA-sourced loans "you don't even recover the cost of
  valuation and legal and account fulfillment", compounded by zero foreclosure charges. Few lenders admit negative
  unit economics on a live channel.

  SME stuck at **~INR 2,200 cr**; co-lending **16%** of book (from 16.22%), largely gold loan, to be **≤15% by
  31-Mar-2026**. Guidance **unchanged**: 18–20% growth, **13.5% ROE FY27 / 14.5% ROE FY28** (no FY26 ROE guide ever
  given). USD 10 mn infusion; no urgent capital need but a raise seen "earlier than later".
- **Scoreable NOW (all windows lapsed as of 2026-08-13 — verify against actuals, do not treat as forward-looking):**
  (a) co-lending ≤15% of assets at 31-Mar-2026; (b) Q4 FY26 NIM — did the CRR benefit out-run the 25 bps repo
  transmission; (c) Q4 FY26 seasonal fee build (third-party distribution + processing); (d) FY26 exit ROE vs the
  ~12.5–12.6% 9M annualised run-rate; (e) NNPA breaking below 1.0%.
- **_Next Q → check:_** mortgage re-acceleration to 18%+ (an FY27 promise); SME book breaking the INR 2,200 cr ceiling
  (4 → 10 locations); current-account growth finally moving; branch count toward 500; merchant-OD traction (the
  12–18-month clock started Jan-2026); capital raise timing/quantum and dilution; insurance-commission regulation
  landing on the third-party-distribution fee line; ECL transition arithmetic; CLM-1 impact on co-lending economics.

identity.industry: Private-Sector Bank — small/mid-cap retail bank; self-employed mortgage + business-loan lender with a co-lending overlay and a granular, price-led deposit franchise in transition

hero.oneLiner:
DCB Bank delivered its **highest-ever quarterly profit of INR 184.74 crores** while absorbing a **INR 26.87 crores
one-time new-Labour-Code charge** — ex that charge, PAT would have been **INR 205 crores**, ROA **1.01%** and ROE
**14.10%**, i.e. the bank has effectively reached the 1% ROA mark that has been its multi-year goalpost. The engine
is a deposit-cost story, not a yield story: cost of deposit fell to **6.86%** (−10 bps QoQ) while borrowings were
almost halved from **INR 8,400 crores to about INR 4,700 crores**, lifting NIM to **3.27%** even as yield on advances
fell faster than funding cost on lagged repo transmission. Underwriting is simultaneously the cleanest in years —
**slippage 3.08% and GNPA 2.72%, both the lowest in 18 quarters; NNPA 1.1%, lowest in 11 quarters; credit cost 0.37%**
against a stated 0.45% floor — achieved with **fewer employees than a year ago (10,981 vs 11,339)** on 18.5% advance
growth. The open sores management itself names are the **flatlining current account** and the **stuck INR 2,200 crore
SME book**.
hero.industry: Private-Sector Bank — small/mid-cap retail bank; self-employed mortgage + business-loan lender with a co-lending overlay and a granular, price-led deposit franchise in transition

business_model.title: Positioning (investor deck)
business_model.body:
- Vision stated as 'to be the most innovative and responsive neighborhood bank in India serving entrepreneurs, individuals, and businesses'; described as 'A National Bank catering to self employed segment'.
- Attributes listed: granular secured small ticket lending, diversified portfolio (deposits and advances), proven capital efficient business model, stable & skilled management team, expanding branch network and efficient capital consumption.
- Promoted by the Aga Khan Fund for Economic Development (AKFED) & Platinum Jubilee Investments Limited, which hold 16.23%; institutions (including FII + FPI) at 45.76%, with non-promoter institutional shareholding above 1% at 32.20%.
- Strategy points include targeting Tier 2 to Tier 6 locations, limiting corporate, unsecured and lumpy exposures, and creating a diversified, secured and granular portfolio.

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body:
- **Mortgages — ~INR 28,000 crore book, 51% of advances (was 54% four-to-six quarters ago), grew only 12.4% YoY.**
  Three deliberate management actions, all described in the past tense ("I'm using past tense because it's already
  done"): (1) **reorient from Home Loan to Business Loan** — HL is now **less than 50%** of mortgage, and **BL is
  "even more than 60% of the incremental sourcing"**; (2) **raise average ticket size** from "approximately INR 27
  lakhs going to INR 32 lakhs… that INR 5 lakh actually is a **19% growth**"; (3) **shift from DSA-originated to
  own-originated** — "their sourcing, the contribution to DCB Bank has come down. With any national DSA, you can
  check it out." Kutty's framing: "we are **changing the wheels of a moving train**."
- **SME — INR 2,249 crores, the acknowledged laggard.** "we are, in a way, **struggling on the SME book**… it has been
  **stuck at the INR 2,200 crores level for some time now**." The new mid-segment vertical (**INR 3 crores to INR 15
  crores** tickets) is "in an **embryonic stage**" — live in **four locations, six more to come**, NSM and RSMs hired;
  "you'll see the impact of it happening in about, I don't know, **3, 4 quarters' time**… This is a long game."
- **Co-lending — 16% of the asset book, down from 16.22% in Q2.** "largely **gold loan**. Multiple players, but largely
  gold loan based." Growth decelerating by design: "we grew **108% last year**, currently, we are at about **60%, 65%**"
  and from FY27 it tracks total book growth. **New CLM-1 co-lending rules effective 1 January 2026**: "you're aware
  that from January 1 onwards, we have had this new CLM 1 new rules of co-lending coming into play. We see that this
  will continue."
- **"Others" under advances — INR 2,000 crores.** "It's not a large book… the largest component here will be about
  **INR 600 crores, INR 700 crores of loan against term deposit**. So there is a mixed bag of whatever is not
  mentioned in the other products."
- **Deposits.** Cost base "almost INR 65,000 crores". Retail-to-bulk mix **unchanged**: "our ratio of retail to bulk
  remains the same at the portfolio level. And there is no reason to believe that it will be any different" — and the
  rate cut was symmetric, "the reduction in the rate of interest for both bulk deposits and retail deposits, Q3 over
  Q2 is practically the same."
- **Niyo channel — 0.5 million customers.** "a pretty good base of Niyo customers who have come in for us, primarily
  for **low-cost forex card** purposes… cross-selling the savings account and deposit to them is a big opportunity…
  **not a traditional self-employed customer**… primarily salaried and definitely affluent and high net worth."

order_book.title: Order book & pipeline
order_book.body:
Not applicable in the industrial sense (bank). The lending-pipeline read management gave:

- **Demand is borrower-led, not lender-push.** Asked directly whether SME growth is lenders being happy to lend or
  borrowers genuinely wanting credit: "Clearly, I would tell you, **it's a latter. It is that there is a requirement.
  There is a hunger.**"
- **Login volumes at a seasonal peak out of season:** "**December logins are very, very similar to March log-ins.**
  And March is usually a special month… We are neck to neck on that." But: "**Conversion still is a bit more
  conservative.**"
- **Competitive intensity is visible in leakage:** "us losing our good portfolio customers to competition for a higher
  exposure or for a lower cost… If we don't, if you're not able to disburse in time, customers have multiple offers,
  and they're going away."
- **Geographic breadth:** "It's not region specific, **across India**, I'm finding that there is an increased demand.
  And when you speak to DSAs also, you are seeing the same thing happening."
- **System context (analyst-supplied, undisputed):** aggregate system credit off-take back to ~14–14.5%.

guidance.title: Guidance (CRITICAL — verify next quarter)
guidance.body:
> **⚠️ ALL WINDOWS BELOW ARE LAPSED AS OF 2026-08-13.** Q4 FY26 closed 31-Mar-2026 and Q1 FY27 closed 30-Jun-2026.
> Treat every item here as **history to be scored**, not as a live catalyst. Do **not** feed into `triggers.csv`
> (SPEC §3.7 / §10).

- **Growth:** "we continue to remain confident about our guidance of **18% to 20% growth year-on-year**… That remains
  unchanged." Reiterated: "The growth rate will continue in the 18% to 20% range."
- **ROE (the only formal profitability guide):** **13.5% ROE in FY '26-'27 and 14.5% ROE for FY '27-'28.** Management
  went out of its way to correct an analyst who attributed a ~14% FY26 ROE target to them: "I want to clarify, the
  guidance given was 13.5% ROE for '26-'27 and 14.5% ROE for '27-'28. **We haven't necessarily given our guidance for
  this current year.**" Confidence restated twice, including after being pushed on ROA: "since the guidance of 13.5%
  is given, we would like to stick with the 13.5% guidance for the next year and 14.5% the year after."
- **NIM / margin (LAPSED window):** "the upward movement of NIM should continue definitely **till Q1, Q2**, unless
  some repo rate action is done by RBI." Mechanics given: **CRR benefit not fully boxed in** (a Q4 FY26 positive) but
  the **25 bps repo cut is also not fully boxed in** (a Q4 FY26 negative); long-duration term-deposit repricing gives
  "clear visibility of reduction through repricing… all the way to quarter 2 of next year, probably even quarter 3."
  Also flagged: **little further help from savings-account rates** — "Currently, we're at 1.5% at the lowest end of
  the scale… There may not be too much benefit coming from a SA reduction. Unless there is more repo rate cut."
- **Fee income:** "a fee of **1% of the average assets** is something which we should be getting through. Currently…
  we are at 1.1%, but on a go-forward basis, 1% seems very, very achievable on a consistent basis." Core fee should
  "continue at a similar rate… unless there's some regulatory action happening."
- **Credit cost:** running **0.37%** against a "minimum stated goal of **0.45%**".
- **NNPA target:** "get to **1% or less NNPA as soon as possible**… How soon? We'll say, we will get to know soon
  enough." (Explicitly undated.)
- **Mortgage growth (LAPSED window):** "mortgage will come back to a **18% plus growth**, similar to the bank growth
  **in the next full year**" — i.e. FY27; "for the whole of next year, mortgage growth will be higher, equivalent or
  higher to the bank's asset growth." Q3 FY26 actual was **12.4% YoY**.
- **Co-lending (LAPSED hard date):** "I publicly said that our co-lending book **as of March 31 will be 15% or lesser**
  of the total asset book." From FY27: "our co-lending book will grow from '26, '27 onwards **at the same rate as our
  total book**" — 18% if the bank grows 18%, 20% if 20%.
- **Branches (LAPSED / FY27):** only **5 branches opened in 9M FY26**; "**Next year, we should be touching the 500
  branches mark.** So that most likely will happen." Also: "There will be more investment in people coming in."
- **Deliberately NOT guided:** Q4 FY26 specifically — "I really don't comment on the next quarter" / "I don't want to
  comment on quarter 4."

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body:
- **Trade finance as the third fee leg.** Explicitly a hedge against insurance-commission regulation: "we are building,
  we're using this time to **feverishly build trade finance volume**… we have to build a **third, fourth string in our
  fee book**." Rationale: "we do cater primarily to self-employed customers who have a trade finance need." Timeline is
  candidly slow: "we started about 6 months back. The progress is **painfully slow**… over a period of time, you will
  see the benefit of it happening in about **2, 2.5 years**. You will see the snowball turning into an avalanche or we
  hope."
- **Current account — named as the single biggest self-identified gap.** "the lack of CA growth has an impact, of
  course, on the cost of deposit. But **it also robs us an opportunity in a trade fee income and our SME book**. So
  they're all interconnected… We have put up a **very, very senior resource to drive the current account**… we are
  starting from a very low base… **It has been flatlining for too long.** So it's very, very high on my priority list…
  **That we haven't got an action going is another matter.**"
- **Merchant OD / relationship deepening — candidly behind plan.** "We **haven't been very successful on the OD part**…
  on merchant OD, on OD of all sorts, it's **still in the infancy** kind of area. I haven't seen real good progress
  happening yet." Mechanism: going back to existing term-loan customers of 4–6 years' vintage — "**the relationship is
  not built over a phone call**… we're just starting the wooing process." Payoff window: "another **12 to 18 months**
  before it becomes large enough for it to make a difference to our lives." The spillover is already partly visible:
  "the relationship will translate to **current accounts**, which are happening. It is translating a bit in **trade
  finance and OD**… And it's happening **very well in terms of insurance**."
- **Niyo salaried/affluent liability cross-sell** — "each incremental month is a better month in terms of higher
  savings account balance from this Niyo customers."
- **ULI (Unified Lending Interface) as the structural call option.** "The **game changer** could be if something like a
  unified lending interface happens, where **digitization of the land records** happened across India. And then you
  could see a different kind of game coming into play. So we are involved in it… If ULI is anything like ULI, we have
  a very interesting time ahead." (A mortgage lender's underwriting-cost option — undated, unquantified.)

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body:
- **The margin is a liability-side story, and management said so directly:** "the **NIM growth is fully predicated on
  our term deposits and our savings account interest rate going southward**. And we have clarity and we have done this
  playbook once, not once twice, for the last 2 quarters."
- **Spread compressed QoQ and management did not dispute it** — yield on advances −13 bps vs cost of deposit −10 bps.
  Explanation: "The **full impact of the 50 bps rate cut** which happened in the previous quarter **is taken in Q3**,
  the full impact. So what you're seeing is a **lagged impact**. For the 25 basis points repo rate cut, which happened
  in Q3, the impact you will see happening in Q4."
- **Two opposing Q4 FY26 forces (both now history):** "The **full impact of CRR is not boxed in yet. That's a positive
  for Q4**, what is not so very positive is that the **full impact of the 25 basis point repo cut has also not been
  boxed in**."
- **The borrowing swap is doing quiet, heavy lifting.** "our ability to get lower cost of deposit **by giving away
  borrowing, which is more expensive**, is coming into play very quickly. And that's also one of the reasons why…
  the balance sheet is growing only 14%, whereas… we are growing our key areas of customer deposits and loans and
  advances at a much, much higher pace." Also: "the **fall in cost of deposit is sharper than the fall in cost of
  funds**, which basically means that the impact of cost of borrowing is much lesser."
- **The savings-rate lever is nearly exhausted; the term-deposit lever is not.** The 16 bps → 10 bps deceleration in
  cost-of-deposit reduction "is the impact of savings account cut… **you can't cut deeper than what you're cutting.
  Currently, we're at 1.5% at the lowest end of the scale**… you will get the benefit from **TD going forward**."
- **Operating jaws are positive:** "**The jaws are widening** with income growing at 16% and expenses, **including the
  onetime**, growing at 15%."
- **Fee is deposit-linked, not loan-linked — an under-appreciated structural point management volunteered:** "our fee
  growth is **less linked to loans. It is more linked to deposits**… third-party distribution, which is more liability
  linked. Trade finance, largely still liability linked, FX income is DCB remit, foreign remittance… ATM fees, again,
  liabilities. So… **we don't even link it to the loan growth.**"

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- **Recent small infusion, no near-term raise, but an explicit future one:** "you just had this **$10 million
  infusion**… **right now, there is no urgency for capital. But for future growth, we require it.**"
- **Trigger framework is dual:** "We have both as a **timeline based as well as event based**. We are pretty much clear
  of **how much we want to take and at what rate we want to take it**." Conclusion: "at some point in time, **I really
  do see us raising capital** because our ambition and our growth rate will require capital **earlier than later**."
  (Deliberately undated — a dilution watch-item, not a trigger.)
- **Internal accretion is the stated bridge:** "if you're able to **increase your book value by INR 5 every quarter**
  for the last n number of quarters. And in the future also, we are reasonably confident about repeating our business
  in a similar fashion."
- **RWA discipline:** RWA +5% on 7% QoQ asset growth; "Our RWA is well below the 50% mark."
- **Balance-sheet mix as capital allocation:** deliberately shrinking expensive borrowings (INR 8,400 cr → ~INR 4,700
  cr) and accepting a 14% balance-sheet growth rate to protect NIM.
- **Co-lending capped as a risk-allocation choice:** "We're **comfortable with 15%**."

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body:
Confident, unusually plain-spoken, and — notably — **volunteers its own failures unprompted**. Kutty flagged the OD
programme, the SME book and the current account as misses *before* being pushed on them ("we clearly don't have a
working capital problem of, in that sense of the word, but **we do have a work capital problem in the sense that we
don't have enough of it**"; "**That we haven't got an action going is another matter**"). He **corrects analysts on
the record** rather than accepting a flattering premise — twice: refusing an FY26 ROE target he never gave, and
correcting "tax refund" to "interest on tax". He **refuses to guide the next quarter** on principle ("I really don't
comment on the next quarter") while restating multi-year guidance, and explicitly labels a hypothetical as one ("Let
me talk something hypothetical") before quoting the ex-one-off numbers — good disclosure hygiene. He declines to
over-disclose without stonewalling ("there is one way I can answer that without having to reveal more than I need to"
on blended SA cost; "Do we reveal the DSA and organic? No, we don't do that"). The stated philosophy is repeated to
the point of self-parody, deliberately: "**Consistency, predictability and repeatability**… I keep saying this every
meeting" and the closing line — "let's go back to the grind and ensure that we continue to be **predictable and
consistent and boring**." On guidance he is emphatic about not resetting after a good quarter: "**the guidance that
you gave is sacrosanct. And unless something really, really dramatic happen, we don't want to renege on that**" — and
he actively resisted an invitation to raise the ROA bar to 1%, arguing "it's okay to be a bit conservative… Some
headwind will be coming in there." One live-call wobble: he could not immediately answer the RWA question and had to
check ("just hold on… I think it was a scale issue"), then returned with the correct number.

moat.title: 6a. Moat & competitive position
moat.body:
Evidenced on this call — kept here only, not repeated above:

- **Cost position built from headcount deflation, not scale.** 18.5% advance and 19.5% deposit growth delivered with
  **10,981 employees vs 11,339 a year earlier**, and cost-to-income *down* YoY (61.84%) *despite* absorbing INR 26.87
  crores of one-off wage cost. Named drivers: "**organic sourcing vis-à-vis DSA source business, vendor renegotiation,
  impact of digitalization and improved use of AI**". Only 5 branches opened in 9M.
- **Sourcing-channel economics — a genuine durability advantage, quantified qualitatively.** "**the non-DSA sourced
  accounts stay with you for far longer than DSA sourced accounts.** In some cases, **you don't even recover the cost
  of valuation and legal and account fulfillment** by the time the customer forecloses and goes away. And with the
  **zero foreclosure charges** in many cases, there is hardly any recovery possible. So from a long-term perspective,
  this is the way to go." This is a switching-cost / customer-lifetime moat being deliberately bought at the price of
  near-term mortgage growth (12.4% vs 18–20% bank growth).
- **Deposit-pricing power in the making — measured, not asserted.** DCB is converting from a price-leader to a
  service-led franchise: "for the last let's say, about 10, 15 years… **the reason to buy has always been price. That's
  changing.**" The metric offered: "**The difference between our retail peak rate and the composite highest peak rate
  of six biggest banks in India is now down to 60 bps. So we're converging.**" Combined with top-20 concentration at
  **6.61%**, this is the "all three together" test management sets itself: "it is **not 2 out of 3, or 1 out of 3, it's
  all the 3 together, all the time**" (cost of deposit, growth, granularity).
- **ECL readiness as a compliance moat.** Parallel-run for "**Almost 4 years**" (Ravi Kumar) — "**it doesn't keep you
  awake in the night**… It's more or less in line… honestly, when you look at it, there's **hardly anything to worry
  about**." Note the asymmetry management itself flags: "**you will not be able to get a benefit. You'll only, it's the
  higher of the two.**"
- **Underwriting vintage quality.** "**Post pandemic, this is perhaps the best few quarters I've seen in terms of new
  vintage bouncing**" — with recoveries & upgrades at 86% of fresh flow.

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body:
1. **Regulatory risk to insurance commissions — the single largest named threat to the fee engine.** Third-party
   distribution is the biggest core-fee driver and "**a big component in our fee structure**"; the analyst framed the
   risk as regulators "considering **reducing the commissions that are payable on insurance product**… there has been
   a lot of articles on this and I think **some regulatory movement** also." Management did not deny the risk — it
   answered with the mitigation (trade finance). Also hedged the fee guide: core fee holds "**unless there's some
   regulatory action happening, which one is not aware of**."
2. **Deposit-gathering under a changed value proposition.** "close to **3,000 odd employees** in the Branch Banking
   system are now fighting a battle in the market where the reason for coming to us is **not the pricing alone**…
   **So people are finding it a bit difficult.**" M.B. Mahesh's framing was pointed: "in the past, in a slightly
   difficult deposit environment, usually DCB had stormed it, its cost of funds kind of growing faster. **We seem to
   be heading into one such situation again.**"
3. **Current account flatlining** — self-identified, unresolved, and multi-effect (cost of deposit + trade fee + SME).
   "**That we haven't got an action going is another matter.**"
4. **SME book stuck at ~INR 2,200 crores** with the fix admittedly 3–4 quarters out.
5. **Mortgage growth deficit** — 12.4% vs an 18–20% bank; the recovery is a promise for FY27, and it depends on people
   internalising a new model ("people take time to get used to the new way of thinking").
6. **Merchant OD / relationship strategy behind schedule** — "still in the infancy… I haven't seen real good progress
   happening yet", payoff 12–18 months out.
7. **Further repo cuts cut both ways.** The NIM-up thesis holds "**unless some repo rate action is done by RBI**";
   conversely the SA lever is dead without another cut. Yield repricing leads deposit repricing on the way down.
8. **NNPA still above the 1% self-set line** (1.1%), and slippage at 3.08% — best in 18 quarters, but an absolute level
   that leaves no room for a credit-cycle turn.
9. **Capital raise / dilution** is stated as a matter of when, not if.
10. **CLM-1 co-lending regime (live from 1-Jan-2026)** with the book being actively cut from 16.22% → ≤15%.
11. **ECL transition** — no benefit possible, only a floor ("it's the **higher of the two**"), though management is
    relaxed after a ~4-year parallel run.
12. **Zero foreclosure charges** structurally impair recovery of acquisition cost on short-lived (DSA-sourced) loans.
13. **Guidance-vs-arithmetic gap flagged by an analyst and NOT numerically rebutted:** 9M-annualised ROE ~12.5–12.6%
    against the 13.5% FY27 / 14.5% FY28 path. Management's answer was a process answer ("consistency… predictability"),
    plus the correct point that no FY26 ROE guidance was ever given.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body:
- **The fee book is a liability franchise in disguise.** Management's clearest structural insight, offered
  unprompted: DCB's fee scales with **deposits, not loans** (third-party distribution, trade finance, FX/remittance,
  ATM). This inverts the usual bank fee model, means the CA/deposit gap is a *revenue* problem rather than only a
  *cost* problem, and explains why current account is "very, very high on my priority list."
- **DCB is a `Financialization` BENEFICIARY, not a victim** — the opposite side of the trade from the PSU/old-private
  banks in this corpus. Where BANKINDIA and J&KBANK name household savings migrating into equity/MF as the cause of
  their CASA erosion, DCB's largest single core-fee driver **is** that migration ("a very decent third-party
  distribution fee income"). Same macro, opposite P&L line — worth carrying into any cross-bank theme view.
- **The 14% balance-sheet growth is a feature, not weakness.** A screener reading DCB on total-asset growth sees a
  decelerating bank; the 18.5%/19.5% customer growth is being masked by the deliberate retirement of INR 3,700 crores
  of expensive borrowings. The gap between the two numbers *is* the margin strategy.
- **The mortgage slowdown is self-inflicted and paid for in advance.** 12.4% growth is the price of three simultaneous
  changes (HL→BL, ticket size up, DSA→organic) that were completed ~9 months ago. If management is right about
  non-DSA loan longevity, the growth deficit is a timing cost against a permanent lifetime-value gain — and the ticket
  size already moved 19%.
- **Slippage 3.08% being an 18-quarter *low* is a reminder of the underlying asset class.** This is a self-employed,
  small-ticket, secured book; the improvement is real (86% recovery-and-upgrade rate, best post-pandemic vintage
  bouncing) but the absolute level is high by universal-bank standards.
- **Management explicitly refuted the commodity-price → working-capital-credit thesis.** An analyst offered it;
  Kutty rejected it for his segment — the uptick is in **installment loans, not CC/OD**. A useful negative datapoint
  for anyone modelling an SME working-capital cycle off commodity prices.
- **The co-lending book is a gold-loan proxy being deliberately shrunk** — 108% → 60–65% → bank-growth-rate, and
  16.22% → ≤15% of assets. Any read of DCB's growth quality should net this out.
- **ULI + land-record digitisation is an unpriced option on a mortgage lender's cost curve** — management called it
  "the game changer" and said "we are involved in it", with no timeline or quantum.
- **A rare disclosure of channel-economics failure:** on some DSA-sourced loans "you don't even recover the cost of
  valuation and legal and account fulfillment", compounded by zero foreclosure charges. Few lenders admit negative
  unit economics on a live channel.

challenges.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers (listed names)
challenges.body:

> **No web source used.** Unresolvable names are left blank/"unmapped" per SPEC §4. ✅ = already covered in this
> corpus, ⭐ = sector knowledge.

| **Insurance-commission regulation.** Analyst: regulators "may be considering **reducing the commissions that are payable on insurance product**… there has been a lot of articles on this and I think **some regulatory movement** also." Kutty confirmed the exposure — "**third-party distribution is a big component in our fee structure**" — and answered with mitigation, not denial: "we are **feverishly build[ing] trade finance volume**… we have to build a **third, fourth string in our fee book**." Fee guide hedged: core fee holds "**unless there's some regulatory action happening**". | **ICICIPRULI** · 540133 · Life Insurance ✅ · **HDFCLIFE** · 540777 · Life Insurance ✅ · **ICICIGI** · 540716 · General (Non-Life) Insurance ✅ — a commission cap transfers margin from the distributor to the manufacturer | **DCBBANK** (532772) itself, and bank/NBFC bancassurance distributors generally — from our files **RELIGARE** (532915, financial-services holdco incl. broking/health-ins distribution) ✅, **CENTRALBK** (532885, bancassurance-citing PSU bank) ✅ | **Med-High.** The mechanism (commission cap = margin shifts manufacturer-ward) is standard and DCB itself sized its exposure as "a big component". Downgraded from High because the regulation was described as press reports / "some regulatory movement", not a notified rule. DCB's own hedge (trade finance) is explicitly "**painfully slow**", 2–2.5 years to matter — the gap is the risk. |
| **Co-lending regime change + self-imposed cap.** "from **January 1 onwards, we have had this new CLM 1 new rules of co-lending** coming into play"; "our co-lending book **as of March 31 will be 15% or lesser** of the total asset book. We're comfortable with 15%" (from 16.22% in Q2). Growth cut from "**108% last year**" to "about **60%, 65%**" and to bank-growth-rate from FY27. "largely **gold loan**. Multiple players, but largely gold loan based." | Balance-sheet lenders that keep the asset on their own book rather than sharing it — **DCBBANK** (532772) itself by design; direct gold-loan/secured retail balance-sheet lenders in our files: **FEDFINA** · 544027 · Gold Loans + LAP NBFC ✅, **SHRIRAMFIN** · 511218 · Vehicle + MSME + Gold Finance ✅ | **Gold-loan NBFC originators dependent on bank co-lending capacity — LEFT LARGELY UNMAPPED.** The large pure-play gold-loan originators are **not present in `output/concall/companies.csv`**, and per SPEC §4 no web source was used to name them. Resolvable proxies in our files: **Apollo Finvest** · 512437 · Digital/co-lending NBFC ✅, **MOBIKWIK** · 544305 · digital lending via NBFC co-lending ✅ | **Med.** A bank publicly capping co-lending at 15% and decelerating growth 108%→65%→~18% is a genuine funding-supply withdrawal for originators. Conviction capped at Med because DCB named **no counterparty**, and the single largest affected class is unmapped by design rather than absent. |
| **New Labour Code wage shock — INR 26.87 crores in one quarter, unforeseen.** "we have taken an impact of **INR 26.87 crores** on account of the new labour code"; "**We did not know that there is going to be an impact**" / "We **never knew** that there is going to be INR 26 crores, INR 27 crores impact happening because of a Labour Code." | — (no listed beneficiary; this is a transfer to employees / statutory funds) | **Labour-intensive employers economy-wide.** Within this corpus the read-through is to large-headcount banks — **HDFCBANK** (500180) ✅, **PNB** (532461) ✅, **CENTRALBK** (532885) ✅, **KARURVYSYA** (590003) ✅, **SOUTHBANK** (532218) ✅, **UJJIVANSFB** (542904) ✅, **UTKARSHBNK** ✅ | **Med — CROSS-COMPANY READ-THROUGH ONLY.** DCB did **not** name or quantify any other company; do **not** attribute any figure here to those names. Recorded because DCB's own experience establishes that the charge was (a) material to a single quarter (~10 bps of ROA) and (b) **unanticipated**, which is the transferable signal. The recurring drag is small — "**INR 1 crores incrementally per quarter**". |
| **Deposit competition — the price-leader model is being dismantled mid-race.** "for the last… about 10, 15 years… **the reason to buy has always been price. That's changing**… close to **3,000 odd employees** in the Branch Banking system are now fighting a battle… **So people are finding it a bit difficult.**" Gap to the big banks: "the difference between our retail peak rate and the **composite highest peak rate of six biggest banks** in India is now down to **60 bps**." Analyst: "**We seem to be heading into one such situation again.**" | **Large, low-cost, CASA-rich deposit franchises** whose relative funding advantage widens when small banks stop out-bidding them — from our files **HDFCBANK** · 500180 · Private-Sector Bank (universal) ✅, **CENTRALBK** · 532885 · PSU bank, "high CASA" ✅ | **DCBBANK** (532772) and other rate-led small/mid deposit franchises during the transition; the direct beneficiary of high deposit rates is the **depositor**, who is not a listed entity | **Low-Med.** Genuine, specifically-stated and self-quantified (60 bps convergence), but it is a *narrowing* of DCB's own disadvantage, not a clean re-rating event for any named competitor. Kept deliberately low-conviction. |
| **Current account flatlining — a compounding, self-identified inefficiency.** "the lack of CA growth has an impact… on the cost of deposit. But it also **robs us an opportunity in a trade fee income and our SME book**… we are starting from a **very low base**… **It has been flatlining for too long**… That we haven't got an action going is another matter." | **CA-rich transaction banks** that hold the self-employed/SME operating account and therefore the attached trade-finance and fee pool — **HDFCBANK** · 500180 ✅ · **CENTRALBK** · 532885 ✅ | **DCBBANK** (532772) — the loss is triple-counted: funding cost, trade fee, and SME lending entry point | **Med.** Unusually explicit self-diagnosis, and management named the causal chain itself (CA → trade fee → SME). Sector-generic on the beneficiary side, hence Med not High. |
| **DSA channel economics are negative on short-lived loans.** "the **non-DSA sourced accounts stay with you for far longer** than DSA sourced accounts. In some cases, **you don't even recover the cost of valuation and legal and account fulfillment** by the time the customer forecloses… and with the **zero foreclosure charges** in many cases, there is **hardly any recovery possible**." | The **borrower** (zero foreclosure charges = free refinancing optionality) — not a listed entity. Second-order: lenders able to originate organically at scale — DCBBANK itself is buying into this | Loan **DSAs / direct-selling-agent networks** — **UNMAPPED**: no loan-origination DSA resolves from `companies.csv` (the only "DSA" hit, Justo Realfintech · 544542, is a **real-estate** mandate platform and is **not** a lending DSA — deliberately NOT forced into this row). Also: mortgage lenders reliant on DSA-sourced, high-churn books | **Low-Med.** DCB's disclosure of negative unit economics on a live channel is rare and specific, and it is already acting on it (national DSAs' DCB volumes "**has come down**"). Left Low-Med because no listed counterparty exists in our universe. |
| **Analyst-raised and MANAGEMENT-REFUTED — commodity-price-led working-capital credit demand.** Ravi Purohit: "we've seen a lot of increase in commodity prices… whenever commodity prices see these kind of increases, you've seen **working capital across the board go up**. So have you kind of witnessed any… increased demand on SME/MSME side on credit growth owing to this?" | — | — | **RECORDED AS A NEGATIVE — do NOT read this as a DCB tailwind.** Kutty rejected the premise for his segment: "for the SME, the self-employed segment, we are seeing uptick in the, **not in the CC/OD but in installment loans**… **quite contrary to what you're saying**, we are, in a way, **struggling on the SME book**… we clearly **don't have a working capital problem**." Logged per SPEC §4 so the absence is recorded as a **refutation**, not as a gap in extraction. |

qoq_log.body:
- **Q3 FY26 (this):** Highest-ever quarterly PAT **INR 184.74 cr** (+22% YoY) absorbing a **INR 26.87 cr** one-off new
  Labour Code charge; ex-one-off **INR 205 cr / ROA 1.01% / ROE 14.10%** vs reported **ROA 0.91% / ROE 12.73%**.
  Advances **+18.46%**, deposits **+19.54%**, balance sheet only **+14%** as borrowings were cut **INR 8,400 cr →
  ~INR 4,700 cr**. **NIM 3.27%**, cost of deposit **6.86%** (−10 bps QoQ, after −16 bps in Q2) on a ~INR 65,000 cr
  base; yield on advances −13 bps (lagged repo). Asset quality best in years: **GNPA 2.72%** and **slippage 3.08%**
  (18-quarter lows), **NNPA 1.1%** (11-quarter low), **credit cost 0.37%** vs a 0.45% floor, recoveries+upgrades **86%**
  of fresh flow. Core fee **INR 182 cr** (+15% QoQ), fee at **1.1% of average assets**. Cost-to-income **61.84%** on
  **10,981** employees (vs 11,339). Mortgage **+12.4%** only (self-inflicted: HL→BL, ticket INR 27L→32L, DSA→organic);
  SME stuck at **~INR 2,200 cr**; co-lending **16%** of book (from 16.22%), largely gold loan, to be **≤15% by
  31-Mar-2026**. Guidance **unchanged**: 18–20% growth, **13.5% ROE FY27 / 14.5% ROE FY28** (no FY26 ROE guide ever
  given). USD 10 mn infusion; no urgent capital need but a raise seen "earlier than later".
- **Scoreable NOW (all windows lapsed as of 2026-08-13 — verify against actuals, do not treat as forward-looking):**
  (a) co-lending ≤15% of assets at 31-Mar-2026; (b) Q4 FY26 NIM — did the CRR benefit out-run the 25 bps repo
  transmission; (c) Q4 FY26 seasonal fee build (third-party distribution + processing); (d) FY26 exit ROE vs the
  ~12.5–12.6% 9M annualised run-rate; (e) NNPA breaking below 1.0%.
- **_Next Q → check:_** mortgage re-acceleration to 18%+ (an FY27 promise); SME book breaking the INR 2,200 cr ceiling
  (4 → 10 locations); current-account growth finally moving; branch count toward 500; merchant-OD traction (the
  12–18-month clock started Jan-2026); capital raise timing/quantum and dilution; insurance-commission regulation
  landing on the third-party-distribution fee line; ECL transition arithmetic; CLM-1 impact on co-lending economics.
